title: Revisiting Wahba’s Problem: A Certified Fixed-Iteration Solver for Nearest Rotation Matrix Projection
abstract: This paper presents a fast and robust algorithm for projecting 3 × 3 matrices onto the rotation group SO(3), targeting inputs about which nothing is known in advance and the constraints of SIMD execution. Existing methods rely on the singular value decomposition or on adaptive iterations whose cost and failure modes depend on the input. The proposed approach reduces Davenport’s eigenvalue formulation to a secular equation in two bounded parameters, over which the iteration dynamics can be certified exhaustively. The resulting solver runs a provably sufficient fixed number of iterations without branching, handles all degenerate inputs with a single clamp instruction, operates in half precision, and differentiates stably on the rotation manifold itself, where the backward pass of the singular value decomposition is undefined. Extensive synthetic experiments, including a rotation-learning task, demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, and training stability of the proposed method.

title: PoseGravity: Pose Estimation from Points and Lines with Axis Prior
abstract: This paper presents a fast and accurate algorithm for estimating absolute camera pose given a known rotation axis. Existing methods are typically limited to line features, two-point cases, or local optimization routines. The proposed approach provides a complete solution for arbitrary combinations of point and line correspondences, producing a globally optimal result in all cases. The special cases of minimal and planar configurations are highlighted for their practical closed-form solutions. As a theoretical consequence of this work, the general pose problem (PnPnL) is reduced to a function of only two variables. Extensive experiments demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method.

title: Solving Wahba’s Problem in the Complex Domain (Draft)
abstract: This paper develops an exact complex-domain solution to Wahba’s problem. Starting from the stereographic constraints used in SUPER, we construct a structured complex symmetric 4 × 4 matrix whose smallest Takagi vector gives the optimal special unitary rotation. The associated Hermitian matrix gives an equivalent complex eigenvalue problem, and its antiunitary symmetry ensures that the selected vector defines a valid SU(2) matrix, including in degenerate cases. We also give a direct construction from two 2 × 2 complex blocks, a closed-form 2 × 2 Takagi specialization, and the relation to Davenport’s method and QUEST. Experiments verify agreement with the classical singular-value solution to numerical precision. The formulation is exact; it is not intended as a computational improvement over established solvers.

title: Special Unitary Parameterized Estimators of Rotation
abstract: This paper revisits the topic of rotation estimation through the lens of special unitary matrices. We begin by reformulating Wahba's problem using   to derive multiple solutions that yield linear constraints on corresponding quaternion parameters. We then explore applications of these constraints by formulating efficient methods for related problems. Finally, from this theoretical foundation, we propose two novel continuous representations for learning rotations in neural networks. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

title: On the Nearest Special Unitary Matrix
abstract: This paper derives the optimal solution for finding the nearest special unitary matrix to a general square complex matrix under the Frobenius norm. We present both an exact analytical characterization and a faster numerical method. The results are validated experimentally and compared with common ersatz approaches.
